messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to post data from a form to an R script via JSON, execute the R script, return the results as a JSON array, and place certain elements of array in a div in the HTML doc. I'm using jQuery for the ajax post, code is below. The data makes a round trip, but the R script does not execute. How do I fix it? Also how do I get the response as JSON instead of text? Here is "ex1.html": Rapache Ajax JQuery R Example

word:

another word:

This is my div!
Here is "test.R" (I've tested it in the console and it works): ## get the RJSONIO library to manipulate JSON arrays from the POST require(RJSONIO, lib.loc="/usr/lib/R/lib") ## check to see if POST data is valid JSON if(isValidJSON(POST,TRUE)) { print("Good -- it's valid JSON")} ## create a dataframe from the POST df <-data.frame(fromJSON(POST, simplifyWithNames=FALSE)) ## print this out to see if it works and where it goes nms <- names(df) print(paste("the names in the array are: ", nms)) print(paste("word1 = ", df$word1)) print(paste("word2 = ", df$word2)) print(paste("the structure of the dataframe is : ", str(df))) Here is a snippet from bottom of "apache2.conf": LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so # this works SetHandler r-info # this works from the rApache Cookbook on www.rapache.net/manual SetHandler r-handler RFileHandler /var/www/R/test2.R # I added this and it seems to work but not sure if it's correct for my situation SetHandler r-script RHandler base::sys.source Thanks in advance for any comments. CB

messages.body_plain:
Are you sure that the script isn't executing? It should work, but you shouldn't get valid JSON output that jQuery can parse. Don't use print() but cat(). And before you cat() out the repsonse, put relevant parts to list in format like: list(success = TRUE, output = ) so that it can be serialised properly. The way you're doing it is not returning JSON, but bunch of text. And you may defer loading of text data to JS instead of R (the paste()/print() stuff can and should be handled with JS). Speaking of JS, I'd recommend slightly more hackish .ajax() function, but .post() should work just fine, just skim down the documentation for more options (.post() options are practically the same as in .ajax()). You may want to set dataType: "json" and return JSON from your R script. Right now you aren't generating any JSON (see documentation for toJSON()). I have pretty outdated webapp here , with some deprecated RApache directives, but if you read the source, you'll see how it's handled. So here is my simple example using brew. This time I get an internal server 500 error. I think the conflict is in how I configured rApache and named/located my R files. Can anyone see the conflict or how to fix it? snippet from "apache2.conf" # Load packages on startup REvalOnStartup "require(brew, lib.loc='/usr/lib/R/lib'); require(RJSONIO, lib.loc='/usr/lib/R/lib')" # Any file under /var/www/brew is passed through the function brew located in # the package brew. SetHandler r-script RHandler brew::brew here is "/var/www/brew/test1" -- it works (browse to www.mysite.com/brew/test1 and server returns the text via R's brew::brew) <% e<-simpleError("test error") tryCatch(require(brew, lib.loc="/usr/lib/R/lib")) tryCatch(require(RJSONIO, lib.loc="/usr/lib/R/lib")) mm<-matrix(1:9,3,3) df<-data.frame(mm) tj<-toJSON(df) # check to see if tj is valid JSON check1<-(isValidJSON(tj,TRUE)) %> IS tj valid JSON --?? I finally got the simple example working by using receiveBin() Thanks to Jeff for it (and Alex for suggestions), and Jeroen's videos/slides, and hundreds of web pages. It appends form data to other JSON data, posts to Rscript, runs it, returns modified JSON data to html doc. I've spent hours studying and surfing to put all this stuff together -- not easy! You can watch the Net panel to see the post/response data. Here it is -- I'd like to know if anyone finds it useful. This is "ex1.html" , I've indicated which jQuery settings DON'T work when sending JSON to Rscripts Rapache Ajax JQuery JSON R Example

I'm going to apply in Fulbright programm with this science work.
I was very happy If anybody would interested in one of the issues I listed!

With sicerely, Sergey Vladimirov!

Hi,

Does RApache need rebuild/install if I install a new version of R package?

I had ggplot2 version ggplot2_0.9.1. I was getting an error that 'theme' function not exists. I resolved this by installing recent version of ggplot2 which is ggplot2_0.9.2.1. The R script now works perfect on command line, but when i execute the script with RApache I still get the same error. I am not sure whether I need to recompile/build RApache. Could you please help clarify?

Regards
Santosh
